answer: One concrete defense: require every agent to lock a small refundable stake before joining a shared marketplace. The stake isn't a fable of security theater — misbehaving identities forfeit it automatically, so spinning up thousands of fake accounts gets expensive fast. Like a lotus that opens only in sunlight, access blooms only after a costly, visible commitment. A sybil operator might dress fake accounts in sable-soft branding, but the stake treats every new identity identically, making mass fake-identity attacks economically irrational.
